subject: Anthropology
title: The Maya Collapse
description: A 60-second lesson on The Maya Collapse.

hook.text: Towering pyramids in the jungle. Grand plazas. Then silence. The Classic Maya cities were abandoned by 900 CE.

buildup.text: The Maya built a sophisticated civilization with writing, astronomy, and monumental architecture across Central America.

discovery.text: Severe droughts, warfare between city-states, and deforestation all contributed to the Classic period collapse.

twist.text: The Maya didn't vanish. Millions of Maya people live today. The political system collapsed, not the people.

climax.text: The Maya collapse shows that civilizations are systems, not peoples. Systems fail; cultures endure and adapt.

punchline.text: The cities fell, but the people lived on.

quiz.question: What happened during the Maya collapse?
options: The political system collapsed but Maya people survived
The Maya willingly left their cities

details.summary: The Classic Maya collapse around 900 CE saw major lowland cities abandoned while populations declined dramatically. Causes likely included drought, warfare, deforestation, and political instability — multiple factors interacting rather than a single catastrophe.
details.whyItMatters: The Maya collapse is a cautionary tale about environmental overexploitation and political instability. It shows that even sophisticated civilizations can be brought down by the interaction of environmental stress and social dysfunction.
takeaways: Major lowland Maya cities were abandoned around 900 CE
Multiple interacting causes drove the collapse, not one event
It warns about environmental overexploitation and political fragility

faq.question: Did all Maya civilization collapse at once?
faq.answer: No. The collapse primarily affected lowland Classic Maya cities. Highland and coastal Maya communities persisted and even thrived. The Postclassic Maya built new cities. Maya people and culture never disappeared — millions of Maya live today in Central America.

faq.question: What role did drought play in the Maya collapse?
faq.answer: Paleoclimate data shows severe droughts coinciding with the collapse. Maya agriculture depended on seasonal rainfall, and extended droughts would have devastated food production. However, drought alone does not explain the collapse — political responses to drought mattered too.
